clue.text: Endless praise about Henry's church district

indicators.note: about signals the remaining letters are turned around and rearranged
endless means the word praise loses its final letter

parts.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: Someone praising King Henry's church in his home parish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' and 'about' both work on the same word; the rearranged letters give the French capital, then Henry's unit symbol follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A parish is the area served by one church and its priest, a church district.

clue.text: Standard place mostly for the social climber

parts.note: par is the standard or norm, as in golf or 'up to par'

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a venue is a place where an event is held

explanation.surface: A social climber seeking a standard place in society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the final E of VENUE.
explanation.definitionFit: A parvenu is an upstart who has newly risen in wealth or rank without acceptance.

clue.text: Poor player has time out — special teacher required

indicators.note: out tells us the letter for time is removed

parts.note: a rabbit is a weak player, especially a tail-end batsman in cricket

explanation.surface: A struggling player has a timeout and needs a specialist coach.
explanation.walkthrough: RABBIT is British slang for a poor player at cricket, tennis or golf; 'out' removes T.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbi is a Jewish scholar and religious teacher, teaching the law.

clue.text: East African fruit raised, supported by middle of railing

indicators.note: in a down clue, raised means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: haws are the red berries of the hawthorn

indicators.note: middle of picks the central letters of railing

explanation.surface: Fruit hoisted up on a railing in East Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' turns HAWS into SWAH; 'supported by' puts it above ILI, the middle three letters of RAILING.
explanation.definitionFit: Swahili is the Bantu language spoken widely across East Africa, used here as an adjective-cum-noun.

clue.text: Result of spin could be a trap

definitions.meaning: what a spider produces by spinning silk
a web catches flies, so it is a snare

explanation.definitionFit: A spider spins its web, which then serves as its trap for insects.

clue.text: Admits cry of pain over dodgy puns

indicators.note: in a down clue, over places the first piece above the second

parts.note: ow is an exclamation of pain

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable, so the letters of puns are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone groans at bad puns and confesses to making them.
explanation.definitionFit: To own up is to confess or admit something, a phrasal verb synonym.

clue.text: Drop of liquid?

parts.note: read not as a droplet but as a place where water plunges downwards

explanation.definitionFit: A waterfall is a vertical descent of a river over a cliff, a literal fall of water.

clue.text: Early camera that is under a shade

indicators.note: in a down clue, under places the second piece below the first

parts.note: brown is a colour, a shade
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: An old camera tucked away in the shade.
explanation.walkthrough: The Kodak Brownie was a cheap box camera from 1900.
explanation.definitionFit: The Brownie was an early, inexpensive Kodak box camera that popularised snapshots.

clue.text: A late intake at the boarding school, perhaps

definitions.text: A late intake at the boarding school, perhaps

parts.words: A late intake at the boarding school, perhaps
parts.note: intake suggests new pupils arriving late in term, but means food eaten secretly at night in the dormitory

explanation.definitionFit: Pupils at boarding schools traditionally hold secret dormitory snacks after lights out, a staple of school stories.

clue.text: Attempt to make a capture to impress

definitions.meaning: to make a strong favourable impression

explanation.definitionFit: Grab is both a snatching attempt and informal for appealing to or impressing someone.

clue.text: An incorrect statement to the country foments disunion

parts.note: an gives the article A
a lie is a false statement
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: Lying to the nation stirs up division.
explanation.definitionFit: Alienation is estrangement, a separation or disunion between people or groups.

clue.text: Sign, for example, to back the car

indicators.note: to back means the abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: e.g. abbreviates exempli gratia, for example
the Mini is a small British car

explanation.surface: A driver signals before reversing the car.
explanation.definitionFit: Gemini, the Twins, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: One in rut possibly: it's very small and difficult to detect

definitions.text: it's very small and difficult to detect

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A creature stuck in a rut, small and unnoticed.
explanation.definitionFit: A neutrino is a tiny subatomic particle that rarely interacts with matter, so it is notoriously hard to detect.

clue.text: Exposed one in awards expenditure

parts.note: out means revealed, exposed

indicators.note: in places the numeral for one inside the word for awards

parts.note: gongs is British slang for medals or honours
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A recipient's spending is revealed among the award winners.
explanation.walkthrough: GONGS is British slang for medals and honours.
explanation.definitionFit: Outgoings are amounts of money spent, a plural noun meaning expenditure.

clue.text: The stars agree black art is deceptive

indicators.note: deceptive suggests the letters present a false order and must be rearranged

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Astrologers concur that dark magic is misleading.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Bear, Ursa Major, is a large constellation, a group of stars.

clue.text: Request for a reply? Enter name that's reasonable

indicators.note: enter means the abbreviation for name goes inside

parts.note: an SAE, stamped addressed envelope, is enclosed to request a reply

explanation.surface: Instructions on a form: enclose an envelope and enter your name.
explanation.walkthrough: SAE is the British stamped addressed envelope.
explanation.definitionFit: A sane person or plan is sensible and rational, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Squandered University award, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word sounds like another

parts.note: a blue is awarded at Oxford or Cambridge for representing the university in sport

explanation.surface: A student threw away a university sporting honour.
explanation.walkthrough: At Oxford and Cambridge a Blue is the honour for sporting representation.
explanation.definitionFit: Blew, as in blew the money, means wasted or squandered.

clue.text: A drawback arises about most lively party in daring display

indicators.note: about means the reversed letters wrap around the party
in a down clue, arises means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: a rub is a snag or difficulty, as in 'there's the rub'

indicators.note: most means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a rave is a lively party

explanation.surface: A drawback surfaces amid a lively party showing daring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arises' turns A RUB into BURA, which goes 'about' RAV, RAVE with its last letter gone ('most').
explanation.definitionFit: Bravura is a brilliant, daring display of skill or technique.

clue.text: Art class — calm source of strength

parts.note: still means calm and motionless
life is vitality, the energy that gives strength

explanation.surface: An art class described as a calm source of strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Still life is a genre or category of painting showing inanimate objects.

clue.text: The ell-like creature beat its victim

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or beat
prey is a predator's victim

explanation.surface: A creature attacking its victim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ell-like' plays on eel-like: a lamprey is shaped like an eel.
explanation.definitionFit: A lamprey is an eel-shaped jawless fish that clings to and feeds on its host.

clue.text: Bird to miss out catching insect

indicators.note: catching means the insect is held inside

parts.note: to fail is to miss out or fall short
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A bird misses out on catching an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A fantail is a kind of bird, both a pigeon breed and a flycatcher.

clue.text: Novel character from Bath?

parts.note: a Dickens orphan's name, which is also that of a biscuit invented in Bath

explanation.walkthrough: A Bath Oliver is a plain biscuit created in the English city of Bath; Oliver Twist is the Dickens novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver is Dickens's orphan hero and also the biscuit known as the Bath Oliver.

clue.text: Old fortress liable to collapse, holding little weight

indicators.note: holding means the anagram contains the abbreviation
collapse suggests the letters fall apart and are rearranged

parts.note: st is the abbreviation for stone, a unit of weight

explanation.surface: An old fortress liable to collapse under a little weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liable to collapse' reads as a description of the fortress, but 'to collapse' is the anagram signal and 'holding' the container.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bastille was the fortress prison in Paris stormed in 1789.

clue.text: Service the electricity supply? About time!

indicators.note: about means the supply wraps round the letter for time

parts.note: the mains is the main electricity supply

explanation.surface: An impatient demand for the power to be restored.
explanation.definitionFit: Matins is the morning church service, so a religious service.

clue.text: Item for game set up on a wooden projection

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means read upwards, reversed

parts.note: a net is used in games such as tennis

explanation.surface: Equipment for a game is assembled on a wooden peg.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenon is the projecting end of a piece of wood that fits into a mortise joint.

clue.text: Manager is cool, having sun protection

parts.note: super means excellent, cool
a visor shades the eyes from the sun

explanation.surface: A trendy boss wearing a sunshade.
explanation.definitionFit: A supervisor oversees staff and work, a manager.

clue.text: Old boatman on a hard trip

indicators.note: trip suggests a stumble, so the letters are tumbled

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: An ancient sailor on a tough voyage.
explanation.definitionFit: Noah built the ark in Genesis, the archetypal ancient boat-builder and sailor.

clue.text: Excited roar after gold seen in the sky

indicators.note: after means the anagram follows the symbol

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: excited means the letters of roar are stirred up

explanation.surface: An excited roar after spotting gold in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: The aurora, the northern or southern lights, is a glowing display visible overhead at night.

clue.text: Numbers on the church board refer to this

definitions.text: Numbers on the church board refer to this

parts.words: Numbers on the church board refer to this
parts.note: the figures posted on the board in church point to songs in a particular book

explanation.definitionFit: A hymnal is a hymn book; the numbers displayed on the church board identify hymns in it.
